wontfix — the current name handle_principal_get_availability IS the workspace pattern, not a violation.

Evidence: the workspace pattern is handle_<object_snake>_<verb_snake> where both parts may be multi-word snake-case. Examples:

- Email/queryChanges -> handle_email_query_changes (object=Email, verb=queryChanges; both single-word object, two-word verb)
- AddressBook/queryChanges -> handle_address_book_query_changes (object=AddressBook, verb=queryChanges; two-word object, two-word verb)
- CalendarEvent/queryChanges -> handle_calendar_event_query_changes (object=CalendarEvent, verb=queryChanges; two-word object, two-word verb)
- Principal/getAvailability -> handle_principal_get_availability (object=Principal, verb=getAvailability; single-word object, two-word verb)

The bead's own description acknowledges this reading is correct: 'The correct name is `handle_principal_get_availability` would parse as object=principal, verb=get_availability — which actually IS the right reading.' The bead then proposes handle_principal_availability_get as the 'fix', but that would invert the verb words and introduce a different pattern (sub-object naming) not used anywhere else in the workspace.

The alternative ambiguous reading the bead worries about (object=principal_get, verb=availability) is not a real ambiguity — there is no PrincipalGet object anywhere in the workspace; only Principal exists. A reader can always recover the intended parse by looking at the JMAP method registration string (Principal/getAvailability), which is explicit.

Closing wontfix. No code change made.

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'When NOT to file human' rule 4 (might-already-be-done / analysis-shows-no-real-bug): the bead's premise was incorrect on inspection; the right move is to close-with-evidence rather than label human.
description:
**File**: crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/handlers/principal.rs (function \`handle_principal_get_availability\`)

**Divergence**: Every server crate uses \`handle_<snake_case_object>_<verb>\`:
- mail: handle_email_get, handle_mailbox_set, handle_thread_changes, handle_search_snippet_get, handle_mdn_send, handle_sieve_validate
- chat: handle_chat_get, handle_space_set, handle_message_query, handle_chat_typing, handle_space_join
- contacts: handle_address_book_set, handle_contact_card_query_changes
- calendars: handle_calendar_event_query_changes, handle_calendar_event_copy, handle_participant_identity_set
- (etc.)

The single outlier is \`handle_principal_get_availability\` — a verb-after-attribute name. The RFC method is \`Principal/getAvailability\` (camelCase verb \`getAvailability\`), but the handler naming convention is \`handle_<obj>_<verb>\`, which for \`Principal/getAvailability\` should snake-case the verb the same way \`Email/queryChanges\` becomes \`handle_email_query_changes\`. The correct name is \`handle_principal_get_availability\` would parse as object=principal, verb=get_availability — which actually IS the right reading. But the alternative reading is object=principal_get, verb=availability — which is wrong.

**What goes wrong**: tooling (regex auto-discovery, code search for \`handle_principal_*\` to find all principal methods, IDE jump-to-definition by method name) treats the handler ambiguously. More importantly: any future \`Principal/<verb>\` method will collide visually with this one — \`handle_principal_get\` vs \`handle_principal_get_availability\` look like one is a prefix of the other.

**Fix**: rename to \`handle_principal_availability_get\` (object=principal, sub-object=availability, verb=get — matching the \`handle_calendar_event_query\` pattern where the second underscore separates object from verb). This is a non-breaking rename: the dispatcher registration string (\`Principal/getAvailability\`) is unchanged; only the Rust function symbol changes.

**Note**: this is calendars-server-specific but it's the workspace's only handler-naming outlier — flagging here as cross-crate-divergence rather than per-crate review issue because per-crate reviews wouldn't compare against the 95-handler convention.
title: calendars-server handler fn `handle_principal_get_availability` violates the `handle_<obj>_<verb>` naming used by all 95 other handler fns
